gift.text:
Krakow — the Main Square and the szopka contest, a tradition on the UNESCO list.
Wroclaw — little huts on several squares, the "Fairy-Tale Forest" and bronze gnomes.
Gdansk — a market at the Coal Market, free entry.
Dresden — Striezelmarkt, one of the oldest in Germany, since 1434.
Strasbourg — a market since 1570; the city calls itself the "capital of Christmas".
Vienna — a market in front of the City Hall and an ice rink until 6 January.
Tallinn — Town Hall Square, where, according to the city, a tree has been put up since 1441.

gift.title: A traveler's Christmas story
gift.text:
On the eve of Christmas a traveler was walking through the forest to the station and missed the last train. A blizzard was burying the rails, and his phone had died. At the edge of the village one window was lit, and a candle stood on the sill: by an old custom it is set out on Christmas Eve so that anyone on the road knows they are expected here.

The door opened at once. They poured him hot tea, set an extra plate and asked nothing. By morning the blizzard had died down. On leaving, the traveler left his road map on the sill, marked "I was expected here".

They say that since then every route of his has one point without a name. He stops there every winter.

gift.title: Kutia (kuccia) for the Christmas table
gift.text:
Kutia (kuccia in Belarusian) is a barley porridge with honey and poppy seeds. The name covers both the dish and the supper on Christmas Eve.

You will need:
— barley groats — 200 g
— water — 700 ml
— poppy seeds — 3 tbsp
— honey — 3 tbsp
— raisins — 50 g
— walnuts — 50 g
— salt — a pinch

How to make it:
1. Pour boiling water over the poppy seeds, leave for an hour, drain and crush.
2. Add the groats to boiling salted water and simmer for 10–15 minutes on low heat.
3. Steep the raisins in boiling water; toast and chop the walnuts.
4. Stir the poppy seeds, honey and raisins into the warm porridge.
5. Wrap the pot in a towel for 30 minutes and sprinkle with walnuts before serving.

gift.title: Toruń-style gingerbread (homemade take)
gift.text:
Toruń gingerbread has been known since the 14th century: the first baker is mentioned in the city in 1380. This is a homemade take on it — not "the real thing", but it smells just as festive.

You will need:
— wheat flour — 500 g
— honey — 200 g
— butter — 150 g
— icing sugar — 100 g
— egg — 1
— baking soda — 1 tsp
— gingerbread spice mix — 1 sachet (or a pinch each of cinnamon, ginger and cloves)

How to make it:
1. Warm the honey, butter, icing sugar and spices on low heat, then cool to lukewarm.
2. Mix the flour with the soda, add the egg and the honey mixture, and knead a dough.
3. Chill the dough in the fridge for 2 hours.
4. Roll it out 3–4 mm thick, cut out shapes and place them on baking paper.
5. Bake at 180 °C for 8–10 minutes, cool and decorate with icing.
